business_problem: Microsoft needed to expand global data center capacity fast enough to support Azure growth and AI demand, but its cloud supply chain required a more unified data model, stronger inventory visibility, and faster planning and spare-parts processes to scale efficiently and sustainably.
solution_summary: Microsoft and Accenture rebuilt the company's cloud supply-chain operations around a connected data and AI architecture for hyperscale infrastructure growth. The work started with a shared data model for server-rack and network-system information so planners could manage lifecycle relationships, inventory, and deployment from a common digital thread. On top of that core, the team built Azure-based control towers that create a digital twin of the supply chain across more than 34 markets, giving Microsoft a live view of inventory movement and deployment readiness. A blockchain-based shared data structure improves transparency and security, while a small language model enables AI, generative AI, and agentic alerting across planning and execution. The program also replaced third-party spare-parts management with an SAP-powered digital and physical platform so Microsoft could plan, deploy, maintain, and replenish data-center assets through one intelligent operating model.

data_flow: Product, lifecycle, and inventory data is unified in a shared model, then fed into Azure-based control towers that track supply and deployment conditions across the partner network. The platform adds blockchain-backed item visibility and a small language model for AI-assisted planning and alerts, while the SAP-powered spare-parts workflow manages replenishment, repairs, and maintenance for data-center assets across the network.
business_outcome: Microsoft gained a more transparent and resilient supply-chain model for Azure and AI infrastructure growth, improved spare-parts control, shortened planning cycles, reduced inventory buffers, and generated major cost savings while supporting sustainability goals and faster scaling.
